description: contracts/sprint-2.md's CRIT-207 requires gen-solana-wallet.sh's generated address to 'independently re-derive under a SECOND, independent keypair-derivation path (mirrors REQ-201's own cross-check acceptance criterion, applied to REQ-202's new script)'. REQ-201's real cross-check (spawn-orchestrator.mjs::assertRealEvmAddress, called from defaultGenerateEvmWallet) genuinely uses TWO DIFFERENT cryptographic implementations: gen-wallet.sh's own generation pipeline (openssl secp256k1 + a python keccak/sha3 library) versus a completely separate, independently-authored library (viem's privateKeyToAccount) to re-derive the address from the same private key -- this is precisely what lets it catch gen-wallet.sh's own documented sha256-fallback bug (a real, different failure mode the two implementations would disagree on). The delivered Solana equivalent does not meet this bar: gen-solana-wallet.sh itself derives its reported `address` via `solana-keygen pubkey "$KEYPAIR_FILE"` (scripts/gen-solana-wallet.sh), and the test that claims to 'independently re-derive' it (gen-solana-wallet.test.mjs, 'CRIT-207: the generated Solana address independently re-derives... under solana-keygen') ALSO calls `execFileSync("solana-keygen", ["pubkey", tmpKeypairFile], ...)` -- the exact same CLI tool/binary, not a second, independently-implemented derivation path (e.g. @solana/web3.js's Keypair.fromSecretKey(...).publicKey or tweetnacl's ed25519 keypair derivation, either of which would mirror viem's role for the EVM case). The test does have genuine value -- it correctly verifies that the script's own custom bs58-encoding of the raw 64-byte secret key round-trips losslessly back to the same keypair bytes solana-keygen originally generated -- but it provides NO protection against a systematic bug in solana-keygen's OWN pubkey-derivation logic, since that exact same logic is invoked on both sides of the 'independent' comparison. A genuine cross-implementation bug (analogous to gen-wallet.sh's sha256 fallback) would pass this test undetected, unlike REQ-201's real EVM cross-check.

evidence.lineRange: gen-solana-wallet.sh: `ADDRESS="$(solana-keygen pubkey "$KEYPAIR_FILE")"`; gen-solana-wallet.test.mjs: the 'independently re-derives... under solana-keygen' test's own `execFileSync("solana-keygen", ["pubkey", tmpKeypairFile], ...)` call
evidence.snippet: gen-solana-wallet.sh generation: ADDRESS="$(solana-keygen pubkey "$KEYPAIR_FILE")" -- test's own 'independent' check: const rederivedAddress = execFileSync("solana-keygen", ["pubkey", tmpKeypairFile], { encoding: "utf8" }).trim(); assert.equal(rederivedAddress, address, ...) -- same tool used for generation AND for the claimed independent cross-check. Contrast with the real EVM cross-check, assertRealEvmAddress (spawn-orchestrator.mjs), which uses viem's privateKeyToAccount -- a genuinely separate library from gen-wallet.sh's own openssl+python pipeline.
evidence.testName: gen-solana-wallet.test.mjs: 'CRIT-207: the generated Solana address independently re-derives to the same value under solana-keygen (a SECOND, independent derivation path), mirroring REQ-201's ethers-v6 cross-check discipline' -- test passes, but does not test what its own name and contracts/sprint-2.md's CRIT-207 claim it tests.
